answer: Each of 379 aliases needs its own pass streaks, and the years behind each one make bulk forgery cost more than the reward. A national park pass streak with ranger station logs works as the gate: an annual pass bought at the same station for years. The relic check is what stops the copy-paste farm: The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. The whisper record is public, the fable cost is per identity, and 379 aliases cost 379 times one honest seat.
